resources.string: "Alerts could not be loaded (%1$s). This does not mean there are none."
"LibreWXR frames could not be loaded (%1$s). This does not mean “no precipitation”. Try refreshing."
"Current modelled UV index on the WHO scale."
"Dotted grey line. Small discs on it mark the main phases: new moon, first quarter, full moon and last quarter."
"Cells and lightning from LibreWXR within 100 km. Estimated arrival means getting within 8 km if the current movement continues during the next hour. This is not an official alert."

"Storm cells and lightning within 100 km. The letter N marks north, and the scale is at the bottom left of the radar. The red dot is your location. The dashed line with an arrow shows the direction of movement of the nearest cell, yellow lightning flashes as it occurs, and the green sweep is only decorative."
"Storm cells and lightning relative to the location; north is up"
"Storm cells and lightning relative to the location; north is up; scale %1$s km"
"Times from time/expires. The original LibreWXR language is not translated automatically."
"Total modelled cloud cover in percent: 0% is clear, 100% is overcast."
"Total modelled cloud cover in percent. The cloud fills from the bottom according to the percentage."
" Missing data are not filled in from another ensemble."
" Missing UV filled in from GFS without extending the main horizon."
"Rain will last at least an hour"
"The umbrella shows the probability of precipitation. The bluer it is, the higher the probability. It says nothing about intensity."
"Daily total of rain and showers, and snow depth separately. Units follow the settings. The umbrella shows the highest hourly probability."
"Spending a long time outdoors is not recommended."
"Spending a long time outdoors at midday is not recommended."

"The two species with the highest load in the current hour; next to the name is the concentration in grains per m³. Colour by the level of that species. This is not an individual forecast of symptoms; coverage is limited to Europe and the season."
"The ensemble could not be loaded: %1$s. The main forecast remains available."
"Neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for the use of Copernicus information. Modelled data and estimates, not station measurements or an official alert."
"Neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for the use of Copernicus information."
"European AQI from CAMS/Copernicus via Open-Meteo. It is not the US index."
"The phase is derived from the angular distance of the Moon from the Sun at noon on the selected day. The icon shows the illuminated part of the disc and the number its share in percent."
"Phases: new moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full moon, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent."
"The chart shows the height of the Sun and Moon above the horizon in degrees. 0° is the horizon: a positive value means the body is above the horizon, a negative one that it is below it."
"Chart of the Sun and Moon height. Scroll by dragging the tile edge; read values by touching the chart."
"Hourly meteogram %1$s. Precipitation includes snow as water equivalent. The wind rose shows where the wind is blowing to."
"Hourly overview %1$s. A lighter background marks daytime according to the calculated position of the Sun. Press and hold, then move your finger to read values."

"The hourly outlook uses individual hourly model values. The daily outlook uses minimum and maximum temperatures, daily precipitation, maximum wind and gusts, mean and maximum cloud cover, and maximum UV and European AQI."
"The hourly outlook could not be refreshed. The data shown may be out of date."
"This is an approximate estimate of intensity from radar reflectivity, not a measurement. When radar is unavailable, the 15-minute model forecast is used."
"Infrared satellite (NOAA GMGSI). The satellite scale has not been added yet because it has not been verified against the Linux app."
"The interval and step select only existing frames; nothing is interpolated. The forecast (nowcast) remains included."
"The interval is not fully specified; see details."
"The map library (Leaflet) could not be loaded. Check your connection."
"LibreWXR returned no frames for this layer."
"LibreWXR: approximate estimate of intensity from radar reflectivity Z = 200·R^1.6, not a measurement. Open-Meteo: 15-minute model forecast. If a source is unavailable, the fallback is used."
"LibreWXR radar and nowcast · approximate estimate, not a measurement."
"Local extremes of the hourly model, not guaranteed high and low tide times in a harbour."
"Local estimates from the forecast could not be calculated."
"less than 1 km; slow down when driving"
"The minimum and maximum are based on the available hours of today's local day. This is not a measurement at a specific beach."
"The model returned no forecast for the location."
"The model returned no forecast for the location"
"Model cell: %1$s, %2$s; distance %3$s km. Source: Open-Meteo Marine API. Missing hours are not filled in."
"Modelled level relative to mean sea level (MSL)."
"Modelled temperature of the sea surface layer."

"Modelled data, not station measurements.
Open-Meteo.com · CC BY 4.0
Air quality and pollen: CAMS/Copernicus via Open-Meteo
Radar, nowcast, cells and lightning: LibreWXR (librewxr.net)
Alerts: MeteoAlarm, KDE and local estimates"
"Modelled data are not intended for navigation or safety decisions. Tapping a tile opens the Sea screen."
"Modelled data are not intended for navigation or safety decisions. They may not describe a specific harbour or beach."
"Modelled data for the selected location, not a station measurement. A dash means the value is unavailable."
"Modelled UV index on the WHO scale. It is zero at night."

"Models are verified one by one based on temperature data for the next few hours and the proximity of the model cell. Other variables may have different coverage. An already verified model can be selected while others are still being verified."
"MSL is mean sea level, not the local chart datum. A negative value is below this level."
"MSL is not the local chart datum. The trend compares the current model hour with the next one; a change of up to 0.01 m is marked as stable. A missing value is not a zero level."
"Loading failed: %1$s. Pull down to refresh. Any data shown are from the previous load."
"Loading failed: %1$s. Any data shown are from an earlier load."
"The strongest wind and gusts of the day. The wind rose shows where the wind is blowing to. Units follow the settings; colour thresholds are based on km/h."
"Up to 3 charts, each with 1 to 4 variables. The switch determines whether the chart is shown."
"Up to three charts, each with one to four variables."
"Up to the three most significant species by level and ratio to the high-concentration threshold. CAMS/Copernicus model, not an individual forecast of allergy symptoms."
"Highest European AQI of the day, not the US index."
"Highest and lowest temperature of the day. Units follow the settings; colours are based on the original °C."
"Highest hourly UV index of the day. Colour and level follow the WHO scale."
"Gusts are short-term peaks in wind speed. In strong wind they can be much higher than the average wind."
"Some tiles failed to load (outside coverage or a network error)."
": some messages failed to load; the list may be incomplete."
"Low-precision geometric calculations on the device, not a measurement. The chart does not express visibility through clouds or obstacles."
"Nowcast is not available on the server; only history is shown."
"Nowcast could not be loaded; this does not mean there will be no precipitation."

"The uncertainty band is on. The line shows the middle scenario: half of the ensemble runs come out higher and half lower. The band around the line shows how far the runs differ; the narrower it is, the more certain the forecast. The bars of precipitation and UV index and the precipitation probability keep the forecast of the model."
"The uncertainty band is off. The line shows the forecast of the selected model. With the band on you see the middle scenario of many runs and how certain the forecast is."

"Precipitation probability uncertainty band: the ensemble does not provide probability directly, so it is derived from the members. The lower bound is the share of members with at least 1 mm of precipitation per hour, the upper bound the share with at least 0.1 mm."
" The uncertainty band is calculated separately for each variable and hour from at least two different available members. It is the spread of the members, not a guarantee around the main forecast."
"Limit time in the sun around midday and use SPF 30 or higher."
". Read values on the chart; scroll on the title and edges."
"Estimated precipitation intensity over the next hour in 10-minute steps. The bars show intensity, with the time below them. Tap a bar to see the time and expected precipitation intensity."

"Radar reflectivity in dBZ (10 to 80). It is an approximate quantity, not the amount of precipitation in mm/h. Frames marked “forecast” are a nowcast, that is, an extrapolation of the radar, not an observation."
"Official alerts and local estimates from the forecast. The colour corresponds to the severity level."
"Official MeteoAlarm/KDE alerts and separately marked local estimates from the model forecast."

"Controls: press and hold on the chart and move your finger to read values. Move the time by dragging the title or the edges of the tile. If the chart has several variables, tap the legend to temporarily hide or show one."

"Controls: press and hold on the chart and move your finger to read values (blue line). Move the time by dragging the title or the edges of the tile; three days are visible at once. Use the arrows below the chart to change the day, tap the date to open the calendar (years 1950 to 2100), and Now returns to today. If the chart has two curves, tap the legend to temporarily hide one."
" The precipitation probability band is not percentile-based: the bounds are the shares of members with a total of at least 1 and 0.1 mm per hour."
"The period is in seconds, not the speed or height of the waves."
"The period is not the speed or height of the waves. The unit is the second."
"Wave period: the interval between waves in seconds."
"Solid yellow line, with a lighter fill between the line and the horizon. A lighter chart background marks daytime."

"Smooth interpolation does not change the hourly values or the position of the extremes. In custom charts, metres share a single axis; temperature and seconds have their own axes. Tap the legend to temporarily hide a variable."
"The feels-like temperature takes wind, humidity and solar radiation into account. It can differ considerably from the air temperature."
"The OpenStreetMap base tiles failed to load."
"Press and hold on the chart to read values. Move the time by dragging the title or the edges; the charts scroll together. Pull down to refresh."
"Sky cover: clear below 12.5%, mostly clear below 37.5%, partly cloudy below 62.5%, mostly cloudy below 87.5%, otherwise overcast."
". Scroll by dragging the tile edge; read values by touching the chart."
"Surface temperature of the model cell, not a measurement at the beach. The unit follows Settings."
" The request failed or was rejected by the API: %1$s. This is not confirmation of missing geographic coverage."
"Keep an eye on how the situation develops."

"Particulate matter PM2.5 and PM10 are always shown in µg/m³, pollen in grains per m³. The conversion to ppb and ppm applies at 25 °C and 1 atm. The choice applies to the Air quality and pollen screen; the Now screen still shows the European AQI."
"Elevated / high thresholds: alder 50 / 200, birch 50 / 400, grass 20 / 50, mugwort 20 / 50, ragweed 10 / 50, olive 50 / 200 grains/m³."
"No usable sea data is available within 30 km of this location. Choose a coastal or sea location in the top bar."
"The forecast is not available. Pull down to refresh it."
"The forecast is not available. Pull down and try again."
"The dashed line shows the probability of precipitation in that hour. It says nothing about precipitation intensity."
"The original dew point in °C is used for the assessment, regardless of the selected units."
"During polar day or night, sunrise and sunset may not occur; a dash is shown then."
"When air quality is poor or worse, limit strenuous outdoor activity, especially if you are sensitive or have a respiratory condition."
"Mean and highest hourly cloud cover of the day in percent."
"Relative humidity and dew point. The dew point is the temperature at which the air would become saturated with water vapour. The higher it is, the more humid the air feels."
"Relative humidity in %. Below 30% the air is dry."
"The dew point is the temperature at which the air would become saturated with water vapour. The higher it is, the more humid the air feels: from 16° it is humid, from 21° muggy."
"Dew point – the temperature at which air becomes saturated."

"Range 0–100. The lower percentile must be smaller than the upper one. P10–P90 is the band between the 10th and 90th percentiles of the ensemble members; minimum and maximum will be a separate option in the chart."
"Range based on the available temperature forecast of the selected model. A dash means the value is unavailable."
"A rapid pressure drop often precedes worsening weather. It is not an alert, however."
"Solar noon is the midpoint between sunrise and sunset. The moment of the Sun's highest position can differ from it by a few minutes."
"Solar noon – midpoint between sunrise and sunset"
"The bars show the precipitation total for the previous hour as water equivalent, including snow. The bar colour depends on the precipitation type."
"Temperature and feels-like temperature are modelled quantities. Choose the unit in Settings. The dot colour is based on the original temperature in °C and does not change when the units change."
"Temperature, weather condition and day summary always remain. Hiding alerts does not turn off alerts or their screen."
"Air temperature at a height of 2 m."
"Air temperature at a height of 2 m. Choose the unit in Settings."
"Air pressure reduced to sea level and its change over the last 3 hours. The dot colour shows the trend."
"Air pressure reduced to sea level. A rapid pressure drop often precedes worsening weather."
"). This does not mean there are no alerts."
"The trend shows whether the Moon's illumination over the 24 hours around noon is increasing (waxing) or decreasing (waning)."
"The data could not be loaded: %1$s. This does not mean the air quality is good. Pull down to refresh."
"The data could not be refreshed. Pull down and try again. The data shown may come from a previous load."
"The data could not be refreshed. The data shown may be out of date."
"The total is water equivalent, not snow depth."
"Total for the stated model interval. Probability does not express intensity. Nowcast is shown when precipitation is falling now or in the next hour."
"Precipitation total for the hour as water equivalent."
"Precipitation total for the last model interval. The dot and value colour depend on the precipitation type."
"The saved ensemble has not been verified yet or has no current data. The selection is not changed automatically."
"The saved model has not been verified yet or has no current data. The selection is not changed automatically."
"There is no pollen in the available data."
"Seek shade at midday, and use a hat and sunscreen."
"Avoid the sun at midday, and use SPF 50, clothing and sunglasses."
"LibreWXR returned no alerts for the visible area (coverage may be incomplete; official alerts are on the Alerts tab)."
"Wind and gusts at a height of 10 m. Colours and verbal levels follow the Beaufort scale from 0 to 12 and are not official alerts. The wind rose shows where the wind is blowing to."
"The wind is blowing from the %1$s; the arrow shows where it is blowing to; north is up"
"The wind is blowing from the %1$s, %2$s; the arrow shows where it is blowing to; north is up"

"Wind at a height of 10 m. The wind rose shows where the wind is blowing to, not where it comes from. Value colour: yellow from 50 km/h, orange from 62 km/h, red from 89 km/h. This is not an official alert."
"Wind at a height of 10 m. The arrows above the chart show where the wind is blowing to (every 12 hours), not where it comes from."
"humidity below 30%; may dry out skin and mucous membranes"
"The choice applies to this location only. MeteoAlarm and local estimates are kept; the additional alert source changes. Units and appearance are in More → Settings."
"Moonrise and moonset are calculated on the device. If the Moon does not rise or set, -- is shown. Touching the dot shows the phase and the illuminated part."
"Moonrise and moonset are calculated on the device in 10-minute steps, so they are approximate. A dash means the Moon did not cross the horizon on that local day."
"Sunrise and sunset in the local time of the location. The graphic shows an illustrative height of the Sun: above the line is day, below it night."
"Sunrise, noon, sunset and day length of the Sun."
"Sunrise, sunset and day length are calculated on the device for the location and selected date. Times are in the local time of the location and may differ by a minute or two from published tables."
"Moonrise, moonset, phase and trend of the Moon."
"Height of the Sun and Moon above the horizon in degrees."
"Snow depth is in cm or inches."
"Alerts are supplemented by local estimates from the forecast. A local estimate is not an official alert."
"Alerts could not be loaded. This does not mean there are none. Pull down and try again."

"Significant height is the average of the highest third of waves; individual waves can be higher. The direction in the data is where the waves come from; the arrow shows the opposite direction – where they travel to."
"Significant wave height describes the average of the highest third of waves. Individual waves can be higher. The arrows show where the waves travel to; north is up."
"Significant wave height. The arrow shows the direction of travel; north is up."
"Significant wave height; the arrows show where the waves travel to."
"Enter two numbers from 0 to 100 in ascending order."
" · Fallback: the selected source was not available."
"Turn on sea data for the selected location. When off, the Marine API is not loaded."
"Source: LibreWXR · estimate, not an official alert"
"change of +3 hPa or more in 3 hours"
"They are shown only when sea data is turned on and there is a usable sea cell within 30 km of the location. Hiding all of them stops sea data loading on Now."

"The feed contains %1$s alerts, none of which match the area “%2$s”."

resources.string: "%1$s has no data for this location. The original selection is kept."
"%1$s could not be verified (network). The original selection is kept."
"In Europe the worldwide sources repeat MeteoAlarm alerts, often in English. Sources are not merged with each other."
"No alert source is switched on. Switch one on using the pencil."
"Official weather alerts from around the world. LibreWXR takes them from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) alert hub and from the US National Weather Service."
"Official alerts from national CAP feeds around the world, collected by a server run by the KDE project. The app shows the weather alerts from them."
" Missing precipitation probability is filled in from the Best match model."
